column3: Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says “Turn your hand” and “the camp”; BSB uses “Turn around” and “the battle.” It leaves the wounded speaker unnamed, where BSB supplies “the king.”
The Hebrew places his death before the description of the blood’s flowing and uses the image of the chariot’s bosom; BSB puts the blood first and calls its destination the floor.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says that he came to Samaria with an active verb and repeats “the king” and “Samaria”; BSB uses passive “was brought” and replaces the repetitions with pronouns or a relative clause.

The Hebrew uses an active singular verb for washing the chariot and a separate clause that the prostitutes bathed; BSB makes the chariot washing passive and turns the bathing into a relative location. It uses a pronoun for the blood’s owner, where BSB names Ahab.
The Hebrew calls the ivory building a “house”; BSB uses “palace.”

The Hebrew uses a singular designation for the shrine prostitute; BSB uses plural “prostitutes.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says that he did not go; BSB makes the ships the plural subject and says that they never set sail.
The Hebrew explicitly says the servants would go “in the ships”; BSB uses the verb “sail.”
The Hebrew repeats “his fathers”; BSB replaces the second occurrence with “them.”
The Hebrew places Samaria in the accession clause and repeats Israel in the duration clause; BSB puts Samaria in the duration clause and leaves the second Israel implicit.
The Hebrew repeats “in the way” for his father, mother, and Jeroboam; BSB combines them under “in the ways.”
The Hebrew leaves the worshiper unnamed; BSB supplies Ahaziah.
